role: AK_TEXT (lines and table rows); MODERN_EDITORIAL (the editor's numbers, brackets, note marks and folio references; his footnotes not reproduced)
comment: Frame 098, printed p. 92: the islands in the sea of Tangier continued: the end of the coast of the island with a town of p. 91, back to its first point; five small islands in a row; another island with a town, followed round its coast; ten small islands; the islands كيوس and حرنيس; and three islands of a quarter of a degree. The editor's running numbers (١٤٠٩)-(١٤٢٤) and the numbers of Suhrāb [٩٤٤]-[٩٥٣]; two passages supplied by the editor between angle brackets. Five lines of the editor's footnotes.

variants: L01: a variant reading of the longitude is مط ه, with a line over the numerals (note a).
L02: a variant reading of the latitude is لد ه, with a line over the numerals (note b).
L02: a variant reading of the longitude is مز ه, with a line over the numerals (note c).
L04: a variant reading of the latitude is لد م, with a line over the numerals (note d).
L04: the point is the same as point 1408 (note e).
L06, L09: a variant reading of the latitude is له ه, with a line over the numerals (note f).
L09: the point is the same as point 1414 (note g).
L09: the letters between the brackets are written by a later hand in the manuscript (note h).
L12-L13: the text between the marks i and k stands in the margin of the manuscript, very indistinct and in part cut away (note i-k).
L13: the manuscript has a gap at the words between the brackets; the editor supplies them after S (note k).
L15: the manuscript lacks the longitude of island 1423; the editor supplies it in view of the position of the neighbouring islands (note l).
unresolved: L09: the bracketed letters may also be read as an alif beside a speck: ابتدأ⟨ا⟩. Transcribed ابتدأ⟨نا⟩.
observations: The description of the island with a town of p. 91 (frame 097, L15) goes on: its coast from point to point, with the degrees and the minutes of each longitude and latitude written with letters under one line, transcribed with {ov:…}, the editor's running numbers in parentheses and the numbers of Suhrāb in square brackets. L01: «تمرّ على صورة الطيلسان تمرّ بعرض لح {z} (١٤٠٩)», along the shape of the ṭaylasān at the latitude لح {z} (point 1409, given by its latitude only); then points 1410 and 1411; L03-L04: «مصبّ نهر وتمرّ الى الموضع الّذى منه ابتدأنا وهو عند طول مه ن والعرض لد {z}», the mouth of a river; and it passes to the place from which we began, which is at the longitude 45° 50′ and the latitude 34° 0′, without a running number; the editor's note e identifies it with point 1408, whose longitude is printed «مه ں» there, without the dot of the ن (frame 097, L15).

L04-L05: «خمس جزائر صغار* مقدار سدس جزء سدس جزء فيما بين طول مز ں (١٤١٢) الى طول ن ن (١٤١٣) وهى كلّها على عرض لا ں», five small islands of the size of a sixth of a degree by a sixth of a degree, between the longitude مز ں and the longitude 50° 50′, all of them on the latitude لا ں.

L05-L09: «جزيرة فيها مدينة اوّلها عند طول مط ك والعرض له {z}», an island without a name, on which is a town; the first point of its coast is at the longitude 49° 20′ and the latitude 35° 0′ (point 1414); then «وتمرّ على صورة الطيلسان تمرّ بعرض لد م» (L06), along the shape of the ṭaylasān at the latitude 34° 40′ (point 1415, given by its latitude only); points 1416-1418; and «تمرّ الى طول مط ك والعرض له {z} وهو الموضع الّذى منه ابتدأ⟨نا⟩» (L09), to the longitude 49° 20′ and the latitude 35° 0′, which is the place from which we began, without a running number; the editor's note g identifies it with point 1414.

L09-L11: «عشر جزائر صغار* مقدار عشر جزء فى عشر جزء وموضعها فى مقدار جزء ونصف فى جزء ونصف وسط هٰذه الجزائر عند طول ن ك والعرض لر ك (١٤١٩)», ten small islands, each of the size of a tenth of a degree by a tenth of a degree, whose place is within one and a half degrees by one and a half degrees; the middle of these islands at the longitude 50° 20′ and the latitude لر ك.

L11-L16: «جزيرة كيوس مقدار جزء ونصف فى جزء» (L11-L12), the island كيوس, of one and a half degrees by one degree, point 1420; «جزيرة حرنيس مقدار جزء وربع فى ⟨نصف جزء⟩» (L13), the island حرنيس, of one and a quarter degrees by half a degree, point 1421; and three islands of a quarter of a degree, «جزيرة مقدار ربع جزء» (L14-L16), points 1422-1424. «كيوس» and «حرنيس» are printed with all their dots; the ح of «حرنيس» has none.

The running numbers run (١٤٠٩)-(١٤٢٤) without a gap; the numbers of Suhrāb, [٩٤٤]-[٩٥٣], stand after (١٤٠٩)-(١٤١١), (١٤١٤)-(١٤١٨), (١٤٢٠) and (١٤٢١), without a gap; points 1412, 1413, 1419 and 1422-1424 have none. Each island or group ends with a small open star with six points, transcribed as an asterisk.

L04, L10: «صغار*»: an asterisk with six solid arms stands after the word, raised like the note marks: the editor's sign for a form against the grammar of the classical language that he keeps from the manuscript (frame 046, L10), as on frame 094 (L03); the stars between the entries are small open stars with six points.

L09: «ابتدأ⟨نا⟩», followed by the note mark h: within the angle brackets stand an alif and, at its right, a round dot of 8 by 8 px, about 24 px above the line, where the dot of the ن of نا stands; the tooth of the ن has not printed. Transcribed ⟨نا⟩, as «ابتدأنا» of L03. The editor's note h says that the words between the brackets are written by a later hand in the manuscript.

L12-L13: the note mark i stands after «والعرض» of L12, before the numerals, and the mark k after the closing angle bracket of L13: the text between the two marks stands in the margin of the manuscript, very indistinct and in part cut away (note i-k); within it, «⟨نصف جزء وسطها عند طول نا م⟩», between angle brackets, fills a gap of the manuscript after S (note k). L15: the degrees and the minutes of the longitude of island 1423, «⟨ند {z}⟩», are printed between angle brackets, followed by the mark l, with the line over the numerals between the brackets: the manuscript lacks them, and the editor supplies them in view of the position of the neighbouring islands (note l). Transcribed with the brackets.

Signs in the text, transcribed as printed: «تمرّ», «وتمرّ» and «مصبّ» (L03) with a shadda; «الّذى» (L03, L09) with a shadda over the ل; «كلّها» (L05) and «اوّلها» (L05) with a shadda; «ابتدأنا» (L03) and «ابتدأ» (L09) with a hamza over the alif; «هٰذه» (L11) with a dagger alif above the ه; «جزائر» and «الجزائر» with a hamza on the tooth; «جزء» with a hamza on the line after the ز; «الّذى», «فى» and «وهى» end in a ى without dots.

Letters printed without their dots in the numerals, transcribed so: «ں» (L04, the minutes of the longitude, «مز ں»; L05, the minutes of the latitude, «لا ں»), the bowl of a final ن without its dot, 50, where L03, L05 and L11 print «ن» with the dot; «لٮ» (L14, the degrees of the latitude), the flat final bowl of the ب without its dot, 32; «ٮح» (L14, the degrees of the longitude), a tooth without its dot, which read as a ن gives 58, beside the longitudes 51° 40′ (L13) and 54° 0′ (L15, L16) of the neighbouring islands. With their dots: «مز» (L02, L04), with the dot of the ز, 47.
In these numerals the editor reads ر as ز, 7 (introduction, frame 196, p. XVII); transcribed ر as printed: «لر» (L11, the degrees of the latitude), 37, a ر joined to the ل with a single rounded head.

The ح of the numerals, «لح» (L01, L12, L15, twice) and «ٮح» (L14), shows no dot in the bowl; the same form is a ج without its dot, 3. Transcribed as printed. The isolated ك, 20, is printed with the small inner stroke of the letter (L02, L06, L07, L09, L11, L12).

Note marks: L01, a after the longitude; L02, b after the latitude and c after the longitude; L04, d and e after the latitude; L06, f after the latitude; L09, f and g after the latitude, and h after the closing angle bracket; L12, i after «والعرض»; L13, k after the closing angle bracket; L15, l after the closing angle bracket. The mark f stands twice, at the latitude of point 1414 and at the same latitude of its return.

Marks not transcribed: L08, a short horizontal stroke, 13 by 7 px, like a hyphen, between the ٤ and the second ١ of (١٤١٨), at the middle of the figures. The page is speckled throughout with small grey points of the paper.
The editor's footnotes stand in five lines below a short rule at the left: notes a-l, one of them, i-k, on the text between two marks. The page number «— ٩٢ —» stands at the foot, centred.
